candidates.title: YouVersion and OneHope launch Bible Loop, a free Scripture app for teens
candidates.summary: A new standalone app in the YouVersion family, built with OneHope, aimed at teens forming their own habits. It offers a verse-memory game with an anonymous leaderboard, Verse of the Day, Daily Prayers, upcoming Learning Loops lessons from partner ministries, and Daily Check-Ins that match devotional content to how a teen is feeling. Available on Android and iOS in English, Spanish, Portuguese and French, with Bible text in 50+ versions across 10 languages. OneHope research cited in the release says weekly Bible engagement drops from 88% at ages 6-9 to 73% at ages 10-12.

candidates.title: Sign language: the final gospel frontier
candidates.summary: MinistryWatch feature on ministries using technology and multimedia to bring Scripture to Deaf people, including a planned natural sign-language animation of the Gospel of Luke (International Mission Board and RevelationMedia) designed to be re-animated into hundreds of sign languages, plus Deaf Missions' Deaf Bible and Deaf Church Where apps. Also notes transparency gaps among Deaf ministries.
candidates.organization: MinistryWatch (reporting on RevelationMedia, IMB, Deaf Missions, Deaf Bible Society)
candidates.whyNotChosen: Strong and in scope, but it is a roundup feature on a long-running effort; the Luke animation is a plan, not a release. Used as also-encouraging.

candidates.title: Many churches lack AI policies despite pastors' support
candidates.summary: Coverage of Barna/Pushpay church technology research: most pastors want guidelines for responsible AI use, few churches have them.
candidates.whyNotChosen: Underlying research predates the window and is about church administration policy rather than a tool that helps people draw closer to Christ; useful as wisdom-concern context only.
